drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Please find attached our initial comments to the Share Purchase Agreement. We have proposed clarifications around the purchase price mechanics, closing deliverables, the scope of the financial statement representation, and indemnity coverage for pre-closing matters and breaches. These revisions are intended to make the draft more complete and workable while preserving the commercial framework.

We look forward to your comments.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: PARTIES. This Share Purchase Agreement is entered into by and between the Seller and Meridian Acquisitions LLC, a limited liability company, as Buyer.
edits.name: Clarify party clause

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, Buyer shall pay to Seller the purchase price for the Shares as set forth on Schedule 1, subject to customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses, net working capital, and any other adjustments expressly provided in this Agreement. Seller shall deliver to Buyer reasonable supporting documentation for such calculations prior to Closing.
edits.name: Add purchase price mechanics and adjustments

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur remotely by exchange of signatures and deliverables within thirty (30) days after signing, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of all conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement. At Closing, Seller shall deliver duly executed instruments transferring the Shares to Buyer free and clear of all liens, together with all other documents reasonably required to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.
edits.name: Add closing conditions and deliverables

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that the financial statements delivered to Buyer are true, complete, and accurate in all material respects, have been prepared in accordance with consistently applied accounting principles, and fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods indicated. Seller further represents that, except as disclosed in writing to Buyer, there are no material liabilities, claims, or obligations of the Company, whether accrued, contingent, or otherwise, that are not reflected in such financial statements.
edits.name: Expand financial statement representation

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, successors, and assigns, from and against all losses, liabilities, damages, claims, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty made by Seller; (b) any breach of any covenant or agreement of Seller; (c) any undisclosed liabilities of the Company; and (d) any liabilities arising from or relating to the period prior to Closing, except to the extent expressly assumed by Buyer under this Agreement.
edits.name: Broaden indemnity protection

receiver.message_back: Counsel, we can accept reasonable closing deliverable and purchase price support language, but your proposed indemnity and financial statement revisions are overbroad: Seller will not stand behind all pre-Closing liabilities or contingent/undisclosed obligations absent knowledge/materiality limits, disclosure schedule exceptions, a survival period, cap, basket, and exclusion for matters reflected in the price adjustment or otherwise known to Buyer. Please send a revised draft reflecting a customary, balanced indemnity package and a financial statement representation limited to Seller’s knowledge, materiality, and the statements delivered in due diligence.

drafter.private_reasoning: We need respond as drafting associate. Must not reveal confidential severance irrelevant. Need produce edits JSON. Need balanced indemnity but protect buyer. Current party Buyer Meridian. Opp counsel wants knowledge/materiality FS, indemnity with survival cap basket exceptions. We can revise with customary but carveouts. Use edits set_clause on para 4 and 5 maybe para 2/3 acceptable. Cover note firm. Use response format.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Attached is Buyer’s revised draft. We have narrowed the financial statement representation to the diligence statements identified as delivered to Buyer and added materiality/knowledge concepts for undisclosed liabilities, while preserving a baseline fair presentation representation for the Company’s books and records.

We also revised the indemnity package to include a survival period, basket, cap, disclosure schedule and purchase price adjustment/known matter exclusions, with customary carveouts for fraud, willful breach, fundamental reps, taxes, indebtedness, transaction expenses, and pre-Closing covenant breaches. This should address Seller’s concerns while leaving Buyer with meaningful recourse for matters that are not already priced into the deal.

Please let us know if you have focused comments on the thresholds or survival periods.

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that the financial statements of the Company delivered to Buyer in due diligence and identified on Schedule 3 (the "Financial Statements") (a) were derived from the books and records of the Company, (b) have been prepared in accordance with the accounting principles historically and consistently applied by the Company, except as disclosed on Schedule 3, and (c) fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods indicated, subject, in the case of unaudited interim statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes. To Seller's Knowledge, except (i) as set forth on the Disclosure Schedules, (ii) as reflected or reserved against in the Financial Statements, (iii) for liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date of the most recent Financial Statements and not material individually or in the aggregate, or (iv) as expressly included in the calculation of the purchase price adjustment under this Agreement, the Company does not have any material liabilities or obligations, whether accrued, contingent, or otherwise, of a type required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with the accounting principles described above. For purposes of this Agreement, "Seller's Knowledge" means the actual knowledge of Seller's executive officers after reasonable inquiry of the Company's finance and accounting personnel responsible for the applicable subject matter.
edits.name: Revised financial statement representation with diligence schedule, materiality, knowledge, and customary exclusions.

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. From and after Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the "Buyer Indemnitees"), from and against all losses, liabilities, damages, claims, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees (collectively, "Losses"), to the extent arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty made by Seller in this Agreement; (b) any breach of any covenant or agreement of Seller in this Agreement; (c) any indebtedness, unpaid transaction expenses, taxes attributable to any pre-Closing tax period, or other amounts required to be included in the purchase price adjustment, in each case solely to the extent not actually taken into account in the final determination of the purchase price; and (d) fraud or willful misconduct by Seller. The representations and warranties shall survive for eighteen (18) months after Closing; provided that fundamental representations relating to Seller's authority, title to the Shares, capitalization, brokers, and taxes shall survive until sixty (60) days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Seller shall have no liability for indemnification under clause (a) unless and until the aggregate amount of Losses for which Buyer Indemnitees are entitled to indemnification exceeds one percent (1.0%) of the purchase price (the "Basket"), in which case Seller shall be liable for all such Losses in excess of the Basket. Seller's aggregate liability under clause (a) shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the purchase price; provided that the foregoing Basket and cap shall not apply to Losses arising from fraud, willful misconduct, breaches of fundamental representations, or taxes. Seller shall have no indemnification obligation for Losses to the extent such Losses (i) are specifically disclosed on the Disclosure Schedules, (ii) are actually included in the final purchase price adjustment, (iii) result from matters of which Buyer had actual knowledge prior to Closing based on written materials provided by Seller and expressly identifying the applicable liability, or (iv) are duplicative of amounts otherwise recovered by a Buyer Indemnitee under this Agreement. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate Losses and shall not be entitled to recover punitive damages except to the extent awarded to a third party in a third-party claim.
edits.name: Balanced indemnity package with survival, basket, cap, disclosure/price adjustment/knowledge exclusions, and Buyer carveouts.

receiver.message_back: We can accept Buyer’s framework subject to the following focused revisions: general rep survival reduced to 12 months, Basket increased to 1.5% of purchase price as a true deductible, clause (a) cap reduced to 5% of purchase price, and the uncapped carveout limited to actual fraud, willful misconduct, and fundamental reps consisting only of authority, title to the Shares, capitalization and brokers. With those changes, and with the purchase price adjustment/known matter/disclosure schedule exclusions retained as drafted, Seller is prepared to move to execution.
